findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not match any method
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` but the only definition added in the parent class `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no no-arg overload, so this will not compile. Either add the no-arg variant or pass `context.getUser()`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, disabling conditional UI on the initial login page
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. It is used at line 115 (`authenticate`) and line 137 (`challenge(context, error, field)`), replacing the previous conditions which called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() == null`. The polarity is inverted: for the normal first-time login (no user yet in the context) the WebAuthn attributes (challenge, rpId, conditional-UI flag) are no longer set on the form, so passkey conditional UI / discoverable-key autologin is broken on the plain login and on error re-renders. The condition likely should be `user == null || <re-auth case>` rather than `user != null`.

findings.title: Always-false shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators skips the "no credential registered" short-circuit
findings.body: By overriding `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` to always return `false`, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` never enters the branch that returns `null` when the identified user has no WebAuthn credential of the required type. During re-authentication (user already set in context) the passkey/WebAuthn form elements will therefore be rendered even for users who have no passkey registered, offering an authentication option that cannot succeed. Consider keeping the credential-existence check while suppressing only the allowCredentials list. Also, the method is missing `@Override`, so a future rename in the superclass would silently break this.
